articles.title: Is the UK set to green-light the Rosebank oil field?
articles.summary: Scotland editor James Cook visits Rosebank - the UK's largest known untapped oilfield - in the North Atlantic.
articles.body:
The Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea has been allowed to start production after years of debates and legal wrangling - but a decision is yet to be taken on the Rosebank oil field in the North Atlantic.

Industry bodies argue that the sites could provide jobs and improve the UK's energy security as overseas conflicts threaten supply.

However, environmentalists insist that more drilling would hamper efforts to cut planet-warming carbon emissions as deadly heatwaves and extreme weather affect billions across the globe.

BBC Scotland editor James Cook is at Rosebank, which is scheduled to be up and running by 2027 if approved by the government.

Seventy years of a rivalry that keeps turning, and the 2026 tour

Twelve matches from 22 October: five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests.

India play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests in New Zealand between 22 October and 1 December. It is the largest bilateral tour New Zealand Cricket has ever hosted, and it is set against 100 years of sporting ties between the two countries.

The T20Is are India's first series in New Zealand as double world champions, with Shreyas Iyer now in charge of the side. New Zealand lost the final in Ahmedabad heavily and will want a different story on their own pitches, where the ball swings early and Eden Park's short boundaries punish anything loose.

The ODIs are a meeting of the top two sides in the ICC rankings, a year before the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. New Zealand won the ODI series in India 2-1 in January, so India start this leg with something to put right. Both sides have named separate squads for the first three games and the last two, and Shubman Gill hands the Indian captaincy to Shreyas Iyer for the final two.

The Tests carry the most weight. Both count towards the World Test Championship, where India sit fifth, and New Zealand have won the last three Tests between the sides. India have won a Test series in New Zealand only twice, in 1968 and 2009.

Head to head: seventy years of the rivalry

India and New Zealand first played a Test in 1955. The records in Tests, ODIs and T20Is, and the matches that shaped them.

New Zealand arrived in India in late 1955 for a five-Test series and lost it 2-0. In Chennai (then Madras), Vinoo Mankad and Pankaj Roy put on 413 for the first wicket. Twelve years later the roles flipped: Mansur Ali Khan Pataudi's side won 3-1 in New Zealand, India's first Test series win abroad.

Since then the rivalry has swung in long arcs. New Zealand have won the big knockouts as often as India, and India have struggled to win Test series in New Zealand. Start with the numbers, format by format.

For four decades this was a Test contest decided by home conditions: turners in India, seam and wind in New Zealand. India's 1968 series win there took 41 years to repeat.

One-day cricket brought the sides closer. India have won more ODIs, 63 to 52, but New Zealand have tended to rise for the matches that mattered, and since 2019 those have come on the biggest stages.

India lead 104 to 79 across seven decades. That overall number hides three very different contests.

articles.title: Acidente na Rodovia Anhanguera em Jardinópolis causa morte e fogo | G1
articles.standfirst: Trecho foi bloqueado na noite desta quarta-feira (21) e houve congestionamento.
articles.summary: Um motorista morreu após colisão traseira no km 340 da SP-330. O tráfego no sentido Sul foi bloqueado.
articles.body:
Acidente termina em morte e causa interdição na Rodovia Anhanguera em Jardinópolis (SP). — Foto: Portal CCM – ARTESP

Uma colisão entre duas carretas provocou a morte de uma pessoa em um veículo que pegou fogo e a interdição da Rodovia Anhanguera (SP-330), no km 340, em Jardinópolis (SP), na noite desta quarta-feira (21).

Segundo informações do Centro de Controle Operacional (CCO) da concessionária Entrevias, o acidente ocorreu por volta das 19h44, quando uma carreta da Volkswagen atingiu uma carreta Scania.

Com o impacto, a carreta que atingiu a outra pegou fogo e permaneceu sobre a faixa dois da pista. O motorista morreu no local. A carreta que foi atingida parou no acostamento, e o condutor não se feriu.

Devido à gravidade da batida e ao incêndio, as faixas e o acostamento foram bloqueados, gerando ao menos dois quilômetros de congestionamento entre os quilômetros 342 e 340.

As causas da colisão e a identidade do motorista que morreu não tinham sido divulgadas até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.standfirst: Confira as atividades de campanha da Professora Dorinha (União) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB).
articles.summary: Confira as atividades de campanha da Professora Dorinha (União) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB).
articles.body:
Confira como foi a agenda de campanha dos candidatos ao governo do Tocantins nesta quarta-feira (21), no segundo turno das eleições. Professora Dorinha (União Brasil) cumpriu compromissos em Palmas , enquanto Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) fez campanha em Brejinho de Nazaré, Porto Nacional e Taguatinga.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Professora Dorinha (União) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

A candidata do União Brasil começou o dia participando de uma reunião com lideranças indígenas de diversas etnias. No fim da tarde, esteve no encontro “Todas Por Ela”, onde subiu ao palanque ao lado da senadora pelo Distrito Federal Damares Alves (Republicanos), das senadoras eleitas pelo DF Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) e Bia Kicis (PL), além da primeira-dama do Tocantins, Karynne Sotero.

Durante o evento, Dorinha apresentou prioridades do plano de governo voltadas à proteção e à assistência às mulheres. Entre as propostas, defendeu a ampliação do atendimento policial especializado, com delegacias funcionando 24 horas, ações integradas de combate à violência doméstica e a criação de novas unidades de acolhimento no interior do estado.

“Nós temos a Casa da Mulher Brasileira aqui em Palmas, mas a Casa da Mulher Tocantinense que vai para Araguaína, Gurupi... a estruturação da rede de segurança pública, com o número maior de delegacias, funcionamento 24 horas e, ao mesmo tempo, o programa Antes que Aconteça, o botão do pânico. São ações concretas de combate à violência, aluguel social e a retirada dos agressores das casas das mulheres”, disse a candidata.

Após o evento, Dorinha participou de um encontro com empresários dos setores de engenharia e construção civil, também em Palmas.

O candidato do PSDB participou de uma carreata em Brejinho de Nazaré no início do dia. Ao lado do candidato a vice, Amélio Cayres (MDB), e de apoiadores, ele visitou comerciantes e moradores durante a mobilização.

Em seguida, Vicentinho participou de uma concentração de eleitores em Porto Nacional, município considerado seu reduto político. No local, apresentou propostas do plano de governo voltadas ao desenvolvimento regional.

“Uma dotação orçamentária aprovada na Assembleia de um novo hospital regional de Porto Nacional, que é para atender a saúde da nossa região e que simplesmente se resumiu a um outdoor colocado no anel viário de Porto Nacional. Não lançou-se pedra fundamental, não se iniciou os primeiros alicerces. Então, nós estamos discutindo com a população qual o Tocantins que de fato o tocantinense quer”, afirmou o candidato.

A mobilização em Porto Nacional terminou com uma carreata pelas principais avenidas da cidade e pela Praça do Centenário. Vicentinho encerrou a agenda em Taguatinga, na região sudeste do estado. Durante a noite, participou de reuniões com lideranças políticas e religiosas em Palmas.

Desde o início da campanha, a candidata procurou manter uma discussão respeitosa, apresentando propostas e debatendo seu Plano de Governo com clareza e responsabilidade.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: regras para a reta final das campanhas eleitorais visam evitar abusos e manter o equilíbrio entre candidaturas | G1
articles.standfirst: Esta quinta-feira (22), por exemplo, é o último dia permitido para a circulação de propaganda paga ou impulsionada na internet e também para conteúdos de inteligência artificial nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: Esta quinta-feira (22), por exemplo, é o último dia permitido para a circulação de propaganda paga ou impulsionada na internet e também para conteúdos de inteligência artificial nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Nesta quinta-feira (22), entram em vigor as regras para a reta final das campanhas eleitorais.

O objetivo é evitar abusos e manter o equilíbrio entre as candidaturas. Esta quinta-feira (22) é o último dia permitido para a circulação de propaganda paga ou impulsionada na internet e também para conteúdos de inteligência artificial nas redes sociais. Os comícios das campanhas podem acontecer, no máximo, até as 2h de sexta-feira (23).

A sexta-feira marca o fim da propaganda eleitoral obrigatória no rádio e na TV, da paga na imprensa e dos debates entre os candidatos. No sábado (24), as caminhadas, carreatas, passeatas e a distribuição de material podem ir até as 22h.

Eleições 2026: regras para a reta final das campanhas eleitorais visam evitar abusos e manter o equilíbrio entre candidaturas — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A lei eleitoral também determina restrições para os chamados CACs - caçadores, atiradores e colecionadores de armas. A partir das 22h de sábado (24), eles estão proibidos de transportar armas e munições em todo o Brasil até a segunda-feira (26), depois das eleições.

No domingo, dia 25, a votação ocorre de 8h às 17h, no horário de Brasília. É proibida boca de urna, como a distribuição de santinhos, bandeiraços, carreatas e comícios. O descumprimento dessas regras pode gerar multas e comprometer a prestação final de contas das campanhas. Os eleitores são essenciais nessa fiscalização e podem denunciar pelo aplicativo chamado Pardal, do TSE.

“É ele que vai votar e é ele quem vai trazer para a Justiça Eleitoral as denúncias relativas às irregularidades nas campanhas. Então, sim, o eleitor baixa o aplicativo Pardal, tira a foto da propaganda irregular na rua, afixada, por exemplo, em equipamentos públicos ou fora do horário permitido, e isso vai ser tratado na comissão de propaganda irregular quanto ao poder de polícia, ir lá e retirar, e também em relação às multas, no aspecto judicial depois, no julgamento dessas representações”, explica Marília Guedes, juíza eleitoral TRE/DF.

articles.title: Prefeito de Nova York chama fim da escala 6x1 de 'passo histórico' no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeito de Nova York relembrou encontro com Lula e disse que construir um futuro melhor passa por devolver às pessoas mais tempo fora do trabalho.
articles.summary: Prefeito de Nova York relembrou encontro com Lula e disse que construir um futuro melhor passa por devolver às pessoas mais tempo fora do trabalho.
articles.body:
Presidente Lula e prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, durante encontro na casa do embaixador brasileiro na ONU, Sérgio Danese, em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 21 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Adam Gray/Pool via REUTERS

O prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, elogiou nesta quarta-feira (21) a aprovação das novas regras trabalhistas que preveem o fim da escala 6x1 e a redução gradual da jornada semanal no Brasil. Em publicação nas redes sociais, ele atribuiu a medida a uma conquista dos trabalhadores brasileiros e lembrou uma conversa que teve recentemente com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

"Há um mês, sentei-me com o presidente Lula para discutir como o governo pode servir aos pobres e trabalhadores. Semanas depois, o Brasil deu um passo histórico: uma semana de trabalho de 40 horas, pelo menos dois dias de folga e sem cortes salariais para mais de 30 milhões de trabalhadores", escreveu o prefeito.

Na publicação, Mamdani afirmou que trabalhadores brasileiros e norte-americanos travaram lutas históricas por jornadas menores e mais tempo de descanso.

"Os trabalhadores lutaram por décadas para conquistar a semana de trabalho de cinco dias na América. Os trabalhadores brasileiros também lutaram por esta vitória. Parabenizo-os por esta conquista", declarou.

O prefeito também defendeu a redução do tempo de trabalho como forma de melhorar a qualidade de vida.

"As pessoas que trabalham merecem tempo para viver, não apenas para trabalhar. Construir um futuro melhor significa devolver às pessoas mais de suas vidas", disse.

Publicação do prefeito de Nova York sobre fim da escala 6x1 no Brasil. — Foto: Reprodução/X

A menção a Lula ocorre cerca de um mês após o encontro entre os dois em Nova York , na véspera da Assembleia Geral da ONU. Na ocasião, o presidente brasileiro e o prefeito trocaram presentes, incluindo uma camisa do Corinthians entregue por Lula a Mamdani.

Durante a reunião, realizada na residência do embaixador brasileiro na ONU, os dois conversaram sobre pobreza, desigualdade e o custo de vida nas grandes cidades. Mamdani afirmou que Nova York é uma das cidades mais caras do mundo e disse que um em cada quatro moradores vive na pobreza. Ele também classificou Lula como uma "fonte de inspiração".

Naquele encontro, Lula afirmou esperar que o prefeito se tornasse um "soldado" no combate à pobreza e à invisibilidade social.

A manifestação de Mamdani ocorre poucos dias após a promulgação da PEC que prevê o fim da escala 6x1 . A emenda constitucional garante dois dias de descanso remunerado por semana e estabelece uma redução gradual da jornada de trabalho sem diminuição salarial.

Pelas regras aprovadas, as mudanças começam a valer em 16 de dezembro de 2026. A partir dessa data, a jornada máxima passará de 44 para 42 horas semanais, com dois dias de descanso remunerado por semana. Em 16 de dezembro de 2027, o limite será reduzido para 40 horas semanais.

Segundo o texto promulgado pelo Congresso, a redução ocorrerá sem corte de salários e deverá beneficiar 14,8 milhões de trabalhadores brasileiros.

articles.title: How a domestic dispute led 2 brothers to strangle their father, burn his body with petrol and bury it near home
articles.summary: Jhunjhunu police arrested brothers Shiv and Deependra Jangid for allegedly killing father Jugal Kishore, burning the body with petrol and burying it.
articles.body: JHUNJHUNU: Police Tuesday arrested two brothers for allegedly strangling their father, burning his body with petrol and burying it near their house at Tara ka Bas village in Jhunjhunu’s Sultana police station area.Sultana SHO Ramniwas said preliminary investigation indicated that Shiv and Deependra had allegedly killed their father, Jugal Kishore Jangid, during a domestic dispute. They allegedly told relatives and others that he had gone to Mumbai and claimed that the buried remains belonged to an unidentified person.Police received information on Oct 17, 2026 about a body buried near a house in the village. An FSL team examined the site, and the body was identified as Jugal Kishore.His cousin, Pawan Kumar, lodged a report on Oct 18. Questioning of family members revealed that Jugal Kishore had been missing for six to seven days. Police registered a case on suspicion that he had been murdered and buried.Chirawa DSP Gaurav Gurjar inspected the scene, while MIU and MOB teams collected scientific evidence. A team led by Ramniwas investigated the case using technical evidence and intelligence inputs.Police said suspicion subsequently fell on Jugal Kishore’s sons. They were detained for questioning and arrested after facts concerning the incident emerged.According to Ramniwas, the brothers allegedly strangled their father in a fit of rage, poured petrol on his body, burnt it and buried it in the soil near their house. The killing was believed to have occurred five to seven days before the body was found.A court remanded both accused in police custody for three days. articles.summary: Levantamento mostra que Uberlândia, Uberaba e Patrocínio lideraram o comparecimento eleitoral no 1º turno das Eleições 2026, superando cidades menores da região.
articles.body:
Em Uberlândia, o 2º turno de 2022 teve menos faltosos que primeiro; uma inversão histórica — Foto: Fabiane de Paula/ SVM

Em uma eleição marcada nacionalmente por níveis elevados de abstenção , os principais colégios eleitorais do Triângulo Mineiro, Alto Paranaíba e Noroeste de Minas conseguiram reter uma parcela maior de eleitores nas urnas , com menor proporção de eleitores ausentes, no primeiro turno das Eleições 2026.

O g1 realizou o levantamento dos dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) nas cidades com mais de 50 mil habitantes nas regiões . O ranking mostra que as menores taxas de abstenção foram registradas em Patrocínio , Uberlândia e Uberaba . Juntas, elas reúnem uma parcela expressiva do eleitorado regional e conseguiram manter índices de comparecimento superiores aos observados em outros municípios do recorte. Confira o gráfico mais abaixo.

Nos dias que antecedem a decisão do próximo presidente do Brasil, o g1 apresenta uma série de reportagens com ângulos distintos sobre a abstenção no Triângulo Mineiro, Alto Paranaíba e Noroeste de Minas, sobre:

O resultado chama a atenção porque contraria uma percepção comum de que centros urbanos maiores tendem a ter mais dificuldade para mobilizar os eleitores. Os números indicam justamente o contrário: nas maiores concentrações populacionais da região, a participação foi mais elevada .

A diferença entre o município com maior e o com menor índice de abstenção chegou a 7,59 pontos percentuais .

Especialista alerta sobre perigo de abstenção

A média de abstenção no primeiro turno entre as cidades com mais de 50 mil habitantes nas regiões é de 22,68%. Um índice próximo do cenário nacional de quase 33,5 milhões de eleitores . Em todo Brasil, 21,08% dos eleitores não compareceram para votação .

Um dos assuntos abordados foi sobre abstenções, votos nulos e brancos na cidade durante os últimos pleitos gerais.

A pesquisadora Alecilda Oliveira já alertava sobre o crescimento das abstenções.

"Esse dado mostra uma democracia participativa em erosão. É um processo que precisa ser observado com atenção."

Segundo ela, os números podem refletir um fenômeno mais amplo de descrença na política. "Existe um sentimento antipolítica que vem crescendo há anos. Isso ajuda a explicar por que parte das pessoas deixa de enxergar valor na participação eleitoral", afirmou Alecilda Oliveira.

articles.title: US ambassador to Turkiye: Rethinking US role in the Middle East
articles.summary: Tom Barrack says Washington’s relationship with the Middle East needs to change from one of control to one of support.
articles.body:
The United States ambassador to Turkiye and special presidential envoy for Syria and Iraq says Washington’s relationship with the countries in the Middle East needs to change.

Tom Barrack says the US no longer seeks to dominate the region.

He won’t say whether the war in Iran was a mistake – but acknowledges the instability it caused has led to unintended consequences.

Barrack says President Donald Trump is against what he calls “forever wars”, and ending the US-Israel war on Iran will require a major compromise. According to him, each side will have to accept conditions it does not like.

However, he is worried that growing tensions could lead to miscalculation.

Barrack says trust is lacking between Washington and Tehran, and that is hampering talks to agree on a deal.

He tells Al Jazeera that countries in the region should not depend on the US to solve their problems and that they need to look out for themselves. He insists the Trump administration has not abandoned the region, but is rather re-examining its role.

Barrack admits that years of US involvement in the region demonstrate that intervention and regime change do not work. He says it is time to put down the guns and resolve disputes through negotiations and mutual respect.

articles.body: In remarks likely to ruffle feathers in India, Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu called for an early convening of the Saarc summit during his visit to Pakistan, saying Male is ready to work with other member-states to make the summit happen.The summit, which was to take place in Islamabad in 2016, was called off because of the cross-border Uri terrorist attack in J&K and the process has remained stalled since then. India maintains that regional cooperation under Saarc is possible only in an atmosphere free of terror and it’s up to Pakistan to create that environment.Maldives and Pak sign 20 MoUs including defence, maritime cooperationI believe that through this organisation, we can work together to find solutions to the challenges facing the countries of this region,” said Muizzu in Islamabad during what was the first visit by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in over a decade.“The Maldives stands ready to consult with member countries on resuming Saarc’s work. Through sustained dialogue, trust and understanding, we can strengthen cooperation within Saarc,” he said.The visit also saw the two sides signing 20 MoUs, including in areas like defence and maritime cooperation that will be of concern to India.This is not the first time though that Muizzu has called for revival of Saarc. In his independence day speech this year, Muizzu had also offered to act as a mediator between India and Pakistan to advance talks for an early leaders’ summit.The last Saarc summit was held in 2014 in Nepal. Member-states like the Maldives, Bangladesh and Nepal have from time-to-time sought revival of the summit.In its response, India has always blamed Pakistan for blocking the initiative for a connected and integrated South Asia.“India favours strong regional cooperation and has been working towards it for several decades. articles.title: Mumbai clears 77 of 231 garbage hotspots, targets 128 by year-end
articles.summary: MUMBAI: From reclaiming footpaths riddled with illegal construction debris to creating seating areas for senior citizens, BMC is attempting to turn
articles.body: MUMBAI: From reclaiming footpaths riddled with illegal construction debris to creating seating areas for senior citizens, BMC is attempting to turn Mumbai's garbage-vulnerable points (GVPs) into usable public spaces.Of the 231 such spots identified across the city till April this year, 77 had been cleaned up by Oct, leaving 154. The civic body has set a target of bringing the number down to 128 by Dec. A garbage-vulnerable point is a location where waste is repeatedly dumped and accumulates over a prolonged period, requiring intervention by the concerned civic ward to address the problem.Two such locations are in Sewri and Chinchpokli areas wherein the civic body is attempting to go beyond simply clearing accumulated waste. At Zakaria Bunder Road along Eastern Freeway, a spot where construction and demolition (C&D) waste was being dumped illegally at night has been cleared, restoring the footpath for safer and more convenient pedestrian movement.A CCTV now has been placed there as well. Shiv Sena UBT corporator Bharti Pednekar said at Chinchpokli, another GVP has been eliminated and the space converted into a seating area, with benches now placed at the site. "The facility gives elderly residents a place to sit, relax and interact with one another. We have even spoken to the locals to ensure they dispose waste the correct way," she said.However, sustaining these improvements remains a challenge, particularly in neighbourhoods where dumping garbage at the same location has become a long-standing practice. Assistant Municipal Commissioner of F-South ward Vrushali Ingole said eliminating GVPs requires residents to cooperate with the civic body and hand over their waste directly to BMC collection vans rather than dumping it on roadsides."The ward first deploys staff at an identified spot for a few days to understand where the garbage is coming from. Our teams then approach residents in the surrounding areas, explain the need to stop dumping waste at the location and seek their cooperation. We have also arranged for collection vans to stop at convenient points so residents can hand over their garbage directly," she said.Sanjay Mohite, assistant engineer of F-South's solid waste department, said at the Eastern Freeway location, the ward set up a Solid Waste Management chowky to ensure staff presence and prevent the spot from reverting to a dumping ground. articles.title: ‘Anti-Indian hate is exploding’: US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi flags rising anti-Hindu hate online
articles.summary: US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi on Wednesday (local time) raised concerns over rising anti-Indian, anti-South Asian and anti-Hindu hate on social
articles.body: US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi on Wednesday (local time) raised concerns over rising anti-Indian, anti-South Asian and anti-Hindu hate on social media, accusing major technology companies of profiting from online hostility and calling on Congress to hold them accountable.In a post on X, Krishnamoorthi said, "Anti-Indian hate is exploding on social media, and Big Tech is profiting from it. These companies have no incentive to stop the hatred they help spread. Congress must hold them accountable."He alleged that social media platforms were failing to adequately monitor hateful content, citing an increase of more than 240 per cent in posts promoting anti-South Asian hate.In a video attached to the post, Krishnamoorthi said, "Big Tech is not policing their social media platforms where there's been an explosion of anti-South Asian, anti-Indian, anti-Hindu hate. I'll just give you one statistic: the number of X posts, posts on X or tweets, basically touting anti-South Asian hate has increased by more than 240 per cent over a very short period of time.""And, unfortunately, Big Tech is profiting off of this hate. They have no incentive right now to decrease it. And so we have to at this point, at the federal level, make sure that they face the full consequences of not taking action," he added.His remarks come amid growing concerns over online hostility towards South Asian communities and follow an attempted shooting at the Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois, on October 11.Krishnamoorthi was worshipping at the temple with his family when the alleged attack took place. He subsequently led 105 members of Congress, including every Indian American member of Congress, in urging FBI director Kash Patel to investigate the incident as a potential federal hate crime.According to prosecutors, 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis, a self-identified neo-Nazi, allegedly attempted to shoot a man outside the temple, but his rifle jammed. He fled the scene and later communicated plans to return. A coworker alerted the police, who arrested him that day.Prosecutors allege that Paporakis had authored an eight-page white supremacist manifesto describing violence against people of Indian descent at a Hindu place of worship.In their letter to Patel, the lawmakers wrote, "The alleged combination of targeted racial hatred, a religious setting, and preparations for mass violence demands a comprehensive federal response. We appreciate the FBI’s reported assistance to local investigators and urge the Bureau to ensure that potential hate-crime violations receive explicit attention."The lawmakers also sought details on whether the FBI was examining possible racial, ethnic and religious bias in the Aurora case, whether online platforms or other individuals had facilitated the alleged plot, and what measures the Bureau was taking to address credible threats against Indian Americans, Hindu Americans and other South Asian communities.The letter further stated, "We believe such messaging risks lending governmental legitimacy to racial and religious stereotyping. Federal agencies should make clear that debates over immigration or public safety never justify collective suspicion of Indian, Sikh, Hindu, or other South Asian communities."The lawmakers requested a written response to their questions by October 29, to the extent permitted by the ongoing investigation.Krishnamoorthi flags polarisation in the USEarlier, on October 20, Krishnamoorthi told news agency ANI that the US was becoming increasingly polarised, alleging that rhetoric from senior government officials was contributing to hostility towards minority communities."Well, yes, I do think that the America of today is more polarised than ever before," he said. He added that leaders at the highest levels of government were targeting groups, including Muslims, Indians and gay people, and "villainising people".Citing a controversial post by the department of homeland security targeting a Sikh man, Krishnamoorthi said, "I mean, the best example of that was the Department of Homeland Security tweet on their official account targeting a quote, unquote, 'Mr. Singh,' and saying, you know, 'self-deport or else. And predictably, one week later, a gentleman named Mr. Singh, a Sikh truck driver, was stabbed 17 times, came within inches of his life."The DHS post, which was later deleted, featured a Transformers-themed cartoon depicting an Indian Sikh man alongside the phrase "Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh” and the words “Self deport or find out".Calling for action against hate crimes, Krishnamoorthi said, "And this is what has to stop. If we're going to stop this horrible rash of hate, it has to stop at the top.""And once that happens, I think things become better, although we at all levels of government have to stand together against it," he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: North Korea to resume propaganda broadcasts, South Korea urges dialogue
articles.summary: Pyongyang plans to resume broadcasting anti-South Korean propaganda along the armed border.
articles.body:
North Korea says it plans to resume broadcasting anti-South Korea propaganda along the armed border between the countries, as Seoul has urged Pyongyang to discuss easing tensions.

Kim Yo Jong, a senior North Korean official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Wednesday that North Korea will place loudspeakers along the entire border, following a visit with top military officials to fortifications along the contested frontier.

Kim warned Seoul of “the most horrible and distressing situation” if it continues what Pyongyang calls interference in North Korea’s internal affairs.

She said North Korean tactical units had taken up new positions, and accused South Korean troops of conducting warning broadcasts and firing warning shots at multiple locations near the border.

Seoul said the warning shots were “legitimate and defensive measures”.

South Korea’s military and Ministry of Unification urged Pyongyang to return to talks to resolve differences.

Pyongyang’s new threats are a blow to South Korean President Lee Jae Myung’s efforts to ease inter-Korean hostility, and will raise tensions along the heavily fortified frontier to their highest level since he took office in June last ⁠year.

The two Koreas are separated by the DMZ, established after the 1950-53 Korean War ended in an armistice. North Korea has been reinforcing its side of the DMZ with mines, barriers and fencing since 2024 as it seeks to establish what it calls a permanent border ⁠with South Korea.

South Korea says North Korean mines planted as part of its fortification activity in the DMZ caused a blast last month that seriously wounded two soldiers. Pyongyang denies responsibility, calling the incident a South ⁠Korean fabrication.

Seoul’s Foreign Ministry on Thursday said it would send a letter to the UN ⁠Security Council claiming the blast was caused by mines planted by North Korea and constituted a violation of the Korean War armistice.

The letter will demand an apology from Pyongyang and urge dialogue to prevent escalation, a ministry spokesperson told a briefing.

Since taking office, Lee has pursued a policy of diplomatic engagement and tension reduction with North Korea, despite Pyongyang’s refusal to resume dialogue ‌and its designation of South Korea as a hostile state.

His administration halted South Korean loudspeaker broadcasts and dismantled fixed border loudspeakers last year. Seoul described the steps as key confidence-building measures, after which North Korea suspended its own broadcasts towards South Korea.

articles.title: Dame Judi Dench: I can't do a play, do a film, or read any more
articles.summary: The actress tells BBC Radio 4's Today programme about how her eye condition has affected her life.
articles.body:
Oscar-winning actress Dame Judi Dench says her eye condition has left her unable to perform on stage or read, more than a decade after she was diagnosed.

Dame Judi was diagnosed with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in 2012, a condition that affects her vision and has made it incredibly difficult to even recognise faces.

Speaking to Emma Barnett on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, she said: "I can't be on stage. I can't do a play any more. I can't do a film any more. I can't read any more."

She also revealed how her condition can lead to awkward encounters, saying she sometimes approaches the wrong people "and give them an almost hug" before realising her mistake.

When asked about ageing, Dame Judi, who's 91, replied: "There's nothing to say for it at all. [I] don't think about it too much."

She has enjoyed a career spanning more than seven decades and is one of Britain's most celebrated actors, with a body of work across theatre, television and film.

Dame Judi won an Academy Award for best supporting actress for playing Queen Elizabeth I in Shakespeare in Love in 1999, and became internationally recognised for her portrayal of "M", James Bond's boss. She made her debut as the character in GoldenEye in 1995, becoming the first woman to play the role.

But her sight loss has increasingly affected her ability to work, with the actress previously speaking about struggling to see on film sets and having difficulty learning scripts.

Despite her condition, she has continued to make public appearances and speak openly about adapting to life with deteriorating vision, stating that "the radio has always been important to me".

She was speaking to the BBC ahead of the release of her memoir, called Is It Too Late to Make a Run for It?, which was written alongside theatre director Brendan O'Hea.

During the interview, Dame Judi recalled being invited to lunch by former MI6 chief Sir David Spedding, describing the experience as "very exciting". When she asked where her driver should drop her off, she was told: "No, no, we'll send a car to you, we'll come and pick you up."

However, she arrived about 20 minutes late after the driver struggled to find her house. "I said, 'I'm sorry for being so late because your driver couldn't find my house.' I loved it."

Asked if she had any views on who should play the next Bond, she simply replied: "No."

Dame Judi also discussed meeting US actor Sidney Poitier, who became the first black man to win the Academy Award for best actor in 1964.

She was appearing in Amy's View in New York when Poitier came backstage after a performance. She recalled that director Richard Eyre was in her dressing room, giving her notes, when there was a knock at the door.

She said she felt as if she were in a wind tunnel when Poitier walked in, adding: "It was thrilling."

Asked what she had said to him, Dame Judi replied: "Not much, a bit of an open mouth. So charming. Very tall."

The conversation then turned to her love of Shakespeare. She recalled watching her brother play King Duncan in Macbeth when she was nine.

"He walked on and he said, 'What bloody man is that?' I thought, 'Oh my God, this is for me'. He said 'bloody', did you hear that?"

She also admitted to being "besotted" by Shakespeare's sonnets: "I just love them."

"It's the rhythm of it. It's the rhythm of your heart," she added. "It's the way he's summed up so simply the way that any of us feel about, well, anything."

articles.title: Over 3 lakh Punjab govt employees continue mass leave on day-3 as talks fail; bus staff extend strike indefinitely
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: Over three lakh Punjab govt employees took mass casual leave on Wednesday over pending demands, disrupting work across govt offices.
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Over three lakh Punjab govt employees took mass casual leave on Wednesday over pending demands, disrupting work across govt offices. Talks with the state govt failed to break the deadlock, with employees deciding to continue their two-day protest on Thursday. Meanwhile, the Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC Contract Workers’ Union extended its statewide strike indefinitely, affecting bus services.Employee representatives met chief secretary KAP Sinha at 4 pm after the govt released minutes of an earlier meeting with chief minister Bhagwant Mann, as demanded by unions. However, the nearly two-hour meeting remained inconclusive.Sukhchain Singh Khaira, coordinator of the Joint Action Committee leading the agitation, said work across govt offices, including directorates, was affected. Sahil Sharma, general secretary of the Punjab Civil Secretariat Employees Union, alleged the govt was delaying a resolution by asking unions to reiterate demands already raised in previous meetings.A 39-member delegation of employees and pensioners later met officials but said it received no clear assurances on several demands. They said the govt had clarified that temporary teachers described as regularised had only been given “security of tenure”, without the financial benefits available to regular employees. The delegation also said the govt had no roadmap for Anganwadi, ASHA and mid-day meal workers.The future course of the agitation will be decided at a meeting in Ludhiana on Oct 25. Employees are demanding release of pending dearness allowance (DA) instalments and arrears, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), regularisation of contractual staff, revision of pensions, restoration of 37 discontinued allowances and the cashless health scheme. They have also sought withdrawal of notifications imposing central pay scales and a three-year probation period.The standoff continues despite a Sept 18 meeting between Mann and employee and pensioner representatives, when the chief minister announced an 8% DA hike in two instalments of 4% each from Oct 1 and promised regular monthly meetings.Meanwhile, transport workers extended their strike after talks with a cabinet minister failed to resolve demands for regularisation under service rules, direct departmental contracts for outsourced workers and withdrawal of police cases linked to earlier protests.Union general secretary Shamsher Singh said proposals covering around 1,400 outsourced Punjab Roadways employees and more than 1,700 PRTC workers remained pending. A Sept 21 govt letter had set a one-month deadline to shift workers from outsourcing agencies to direct contracts, but it passed without implementation, he said. A proposal to withdraw cases had also been sent to the Punjab DGP, but no further action had followed despite workers securing bail.The union plans a joint demonstration with Theka Mulazam Sangharsh Morcha in Dirba, the constituency of transport and finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema. Workers from all 27 depots and two sub-depots plan to assemble in Mohali and march towards Punjab Vidhan Sabha and the chief minister’s official residence.Union representatives alleged that shortages of spare parts and tyres had grounded several buses and criticised PRTC management for issuing show-cause notices and termination warnings. However, PRTC GM Operations A S Tiwana said more than 800 of the corporation’s 1,250 buses operated on Wednesday. He said management had proposed bringing around 1,719 outsourced employees under contractual terms.Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh called the mass leave a sign of a deepening crisis of confidence between the Mann govt and its employees. articles.title: Cookies and weapons: Women in Yemen’s Taiz find ways to help the city’s defence
articles.summary: Amid growing threats, a grassroots aid effort has transformed into an initiative to get more ammunition to the front.
articles.body:
Taiz, Yemen – As Houthi fighters tighten their siege on the government-held southwestern Yemeni city of Taiz , women who initially organised food deliveries for soldiers defending the city have begun raising money to buy weapons and ammunition.

The initiatives have emerged spontaneously since the resumption of fighting in early September in the western countryside of Taiz governorate, between Saudi-backed forces of the internationally recognised government and the Iran-backed armed group.

At first, women volunteers came together to bake cookies for fighters on the front lines.

The aim was “to strengthen the relationship between the supportive social base and the members of the national army and pro-government popular resistance forces stationed at the front lines in defence of their besieged city, which is subjected to daily shelling in preparation for an invasion,” said Amira al-Saghir, an activist involved in the campaign.

The cookie-making initiative attracted widespread participation among women volunteers, drawing encouragement and support on social media. It coincided with a broader community campaign to supply fighters with food and other basic necessities, as well as weapons, with people contributing from districts and villages across the governorate.

In Yemen, a conservative country and the poorest in the Middle East, the vast majority of women do not participate in active fighting in the civil war, which began in 2014 . Instead, these initiatives allow women to take part in what they see as the defence of their city against an invading force, and support for the men who are fighting.

After nearly four years of relative calm following a United Nations-brokered truce in April 2022, Houthi forces launched a major ground offensive in western Taiz in early September. The armed group rapidly captured territory along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, including the strategic port city of Mocha on September 10 , expanding its presence around Bab al-Mandeb strait, a vital shipping route.

The Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah, Arabic for Supporters of God, subsequently advanced towards other parts of Taiz governorate, taking control of key routes into the provincial capital and effectively surrounding the city. Government forces have since launched counteroffensives, with control of some areas remaining contested.

The renewed siege has severely restricted the movement of people and essential supplies into the city, triggering shortages of food, fuel, and medicine.

As the fighting intensified, the women’s initiatives expanded. What began with baking cookies and organising food convoys to supply arms kitchens gradually evolved into efforts to buy ammunition for fighters.

Women involved in the initiatives told Al Jazeera that they felt they had been “forced” to act because of the risk of their city falling to the Houthis.

The change began as more rural districts began falling to the Houthis, leading to some donors making their contributions conditional on part of the money being used to buy ammunition for fighters.

Al-Saghir believes the shift was encouraged by information and criticism circulating on social media suggesting that government fighters in Taiz lacked sufficient ammunition to continue defending the city and surrounding front lines.

The initiatives soon took off, encouraging more women to get involved. Among them was Huriya Wabel, a humanitarian activist.

“After we saw that those [Houthi] militias … are waging a war of extermination against our city, we felt that we had to take a serious stand to support the army, not just with food and clothing, but with weapons as well, especially since a siege has been imposed on Taiz and supplies can no longer reach it easily,” Wabel told Al Jazeera.

“We also found many civilians who wanted to participate in the fighting alongside the army in defence of the city, but they did not have weapons,” she added. “So it became incumbent upon us to help by focusing more of our activities on this aspect at this stage.”

For Khadija al-Majidi, the move from providing humanitarian supplies to delivering military equipment is a response to the growing threat facing Taiz.

“When the enemy reaches the gates of your city and imposes a complete siege on it in preparation for storming it by force, and everyone in it – including you, your children, and members of your family – is threatened with being killed, captured, or displaced … then what do you expect from us?” the activist told Al Jazeera. “Did you expect us to carry flowers for the criminal who came from the farthest reaches of the country to destroy our city and kill us?”

When Al Jazeera spoke to al-Majidi, she had just returned from the fighting around Jabal Sabir, the mountain overlooking Taiz from the south.

It was al-Majidi’s second trip to the front that day, delivering ammunition and other military supplies, which she valued at $3,000, to the commander on the front, along with winter clothing, shoes, food, and other necessities.

She said that after more than 10 years of living through Yemen’s devastating war, she no longer felt afraid to visit active battlefronts.

“Repeated visits to the front lines play a major role in removing fears, given what we see on the ground of the heroes’ courage and bravery in defending the city and their confidence in victory,” she added.

As fundraising expands, the women’s department of Taiz’s Supreme Council for Popular Resistance launched a campaign on October 8 , aiming to equip 10,000 pro-government fighters with rifles and ammunition.

The council has called for contributions from Yemenis across the country and abroad to support the initiative.

The campaign reflects the state of the fighting in Taiz, with government forces facing daily Houthi attacks, as they try to conduct their own counter-attacks.

But the longer the siege continues, the more difficult the military and humanitarian situation becomes in the city.

Al-Saghir and al-Majidi both explained that while many of the donations they receive come from Yemenis living abroad, people on the ground are also giving whatever they can, despite the humanitarian crisis in Taiz.

Al-Saghir said one woman whose husband was fighting in the army donated a wedding ring, while al-Majidi recounted stories of other women donating their gold jewellery.

Al-Majidi recalled a woman arriving at her home carrying envelopes containing Yemeni and Saudi currency.

The woman had written on the envelopes, “God willing, we will win. Buy ammunition for the heroes with this.”

articles.title: In Israel election, Palestinian citizens weigh fear against disillusionment
articles.summary: With vote at knife’s edge, Palestinian citizens weigh principle against strategic voting in system stacked against them.
articles.body:
Occupied East Jerusalem – Laila Atamneh, 19, remembers her parents arguing at the dinner table every time Israel would hold an election.

Among the rare Palestinian Jerusalemites who are Israeli citizens and eligible to vote, her father would make the case for casting a ballot for an Arab-led electoral list. Her mother, by contrast, always abstained.

“She thinks it feeds into the idea that Israel is a democracy and Palestinians have the same rights here – only to get extremely humiliated, and then get one of the worst governments ever, and be surrounded by fascists,” said Atamneh, who hails from the neighbourhood of Beit Hanina.

On October 27, the 19-year-old will vote for the first time in Israel’s general election . She sees it as a responsibility to the millions of Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and the Gaza Strip, who will have no say in the next Israeli government but, she believes, bear the brunt of its occupation, ethnic cleansing and genocide.

“I feel like I have to be these people’s voice,” said Atamneh. “Not that one person is really capable of that much – but if this gives them one percent hope, then I will do it.”

But Atamneh, who speaks Arabic, said she struggles to follow election coverage in Hebrew. “I personally feel excluded from everything, that we’re not even a part of the discussion,” she added. “It feels like none of the parties really address our generation of first-time Palestinian voters.”

Her mixed feelings capture the mood among Palestinian citizens of Israel – about a fifth of its population – ahead of the election. Few believe the system will serve them, but many fear another government led by Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, who has overseen Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip since 2023. Whether fear outweighs disillusion may decide a contest in which opinion polls suggest neither Netanyahu’s far-right-led bloc nor the self-styled Zionist opposition alliance will be able to govern without Ra’am and the Joint List, the two Arab-led parties.

And if no one can form a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, new elections will be called – keeping the current Netanyahu government, the most hard right in Israel’s history, in place until then.

For Palestinian citizens of Israel, the animating force of the election is the acceleration of the hard-right assault on Palestinian rights, livelihoods and land in recent years.

“This election comes in the context of the genocide and the ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, and the harsh state policies towards Palestinians in Israel,” said As’ad Ghanem, a political scientist at the University of Haifa. “Palestinian citizens are really afraid. Their leadership is afraid, and this is real.”

For Hanan, a 36-year-old Palestinian Christian in a Druze village in the Galilee, it feels like the danger keeps coming closer to her doorstep.

Israeli settlers residing in illegal settlements in the West Bank last month tried to build an illegal outpost near Majd al-Krum, a Palestinian community in the Galilee. Then, Israel’s far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich released an AI-generated campaign video, in which a Palestinian from the West Bank frantically calls his relative in the Galilee to tell him that “the Jews are coming” to “do to you what they did to us”.

“Acts like these make me more afraid that the settlers will get worse and try to take more Palestinian land,” said Hanan. “This makes me want to vote more, and want to encourage other people to vote.”

On September 23, Israel’s Central Elections Committee voted to disqualify Ra’am and the Joint List – an alliance of the Hadash, Balad and Ta’al parties – before the Supreme Court overturned the decisions. However, Balad’s Sami Abu Shehadeh withdrew his candidacy after the court indicated that a majority of justices supported upholding his disqualification.

Many Palestinians saw this as confirmation that the system is illegitimate; some said the attempt to disqualify the parties was further reason to mobilise either way. “We feel that we are under attack,” said Thabet Abu Rass, an expert on Arab-Jewish relations. “This is why we will cast our vote in a higher percentage.”

Voter turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel ranged from roughly 45 to 65 percent over the past five elections, reaching about 53 percent in the last polls in 2022. A Palestinian campaign operative cited surveys estimating about 62 percent of Palestinian citizens plan to vote next week; he said the aim is 70 to 75 percent, last reached in 1999, when a 75 percent Palestinian turnout helped PM Ehud Barak beat Netanyahu.

“We want to take it there,” he said, noting that a high turnout could keep smaller right-wing parties like Amcha Yisrael and The Reservists from clearing the 3.25 percent electoral threshold, shifting the entire balance of power.

The potential voter surge comes despite Palestinians’ limited, ossified choices.

“Every election, I tell myself that this year I’m not going to vote, because in reality we don’t feel that the Arab members do much,” said Hanan, bemoaning the lack of female representation or new political voices. “But in the end, I always go and vote, because I feel that maybe this time it will help.”

Despite people’s misgivings, Ghanem, the political scientist, dismissed the potential for a mass boycott as “a small point of view” by now. “We are under a real danger,” he said, “and we can contribute to ending this government’s term.”

Hanan said, “I know that voting is like admitting that there is an Israeli country, but it’s here. We can’t be all dreamy.”

The campaign operative added: “The only day that we have the right to be equal with the Jews … is the day of elections.”

The question is what Jewish Israeli parties in the anti-Netanyahu camp will do with the Arab-led lists. Opinion polls have consistently left both Zionist blocs short of the 61 seats needed to form a government – with the Arab parties making the difference.

On paper, that should make the Joint List and Ra’am kingmakers in the election. Yet opposition leader Naftali Bennett has said “The Arab parties are not Zionist, and therefore we will not rely on them.” Former army chief and potential prime ministerial candidate for the opposition Gadi Eisenkot has also expressed refusal to partner with the Arab parties, batting back attempts by Netanyahu to link him to them: “There is no Gadi [Eisenkot] without [Ahmad] Tibi” has become a frequent campaign slogan for Netanyahu, referring to the leader of Ta’al.

With the election at a knife’s edge, Palestinian voters must weigh principle against strategic voting in a system stacked against them. Initially, Atamneh said she considered voting tactically for Ra’am, a religiously conservative party with a Bedouin base in the Naqab, or even the Democrats, the liberal Zionist party – both likelier than the Joint List to join an anti-Netanyahu coalition. But she decided to vote for the Joint List on principle.

“While I can give in to a few things,” she said, “at the end of the day, I have to abide by morals and values I can’t let go of that easily. As Palestinians, we have to support Palestinians.”

In 2021, Ra’am made history by becoming the first Arab party to join an Israeli government when it entered a broad coalition that briefly unseated Netanyahu. But its pitch – that real gains and protections for Palestinian citizens come from sitting in a coalition government – has failed to persuade everyone.

Ghanem argued Ra’am leader Mansour Abbas “gives everything almost in order to get a little bit of budget … but we’re still Palestinians.”

However, Bedouin citizens are expected to largely support Ra’am, hoping it will join the ruling coalition like it did in 2021-2022. “Bedouin political discourse is a civic discourse rather than anything else,” said Abu Rass, with Bedouins focused on “daily survival” – hoping inclusion into the government can bring about “recognising their unrecognised villages, investing in education, and employment”.

‘Before ending the occupation, I want to save my people’

As Ghanem put it, Palestinian politics in Israel is “very weak because we don’t have consolidated political power internally in our community”.

But the political scientist believes the Joint List can make a serious impact on Israeli coalition building like in 1993, when Palestinian parties supported Yitzhak Rabin’s government from outside the cabinet. Wanting to replace Netanyahu, he said, “doesn’t mean that we have to be part of the coalition” – only part of “the whole bloc that wants to replace this racist government”.

Last week, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen expressed a willingness to do just that under agreed-upon terms, including a path to Palestinian statehood and fighting organised crime and violence in Israel’s Palestinian communities.

Despite the campaign rhetoric saying otherwise, Abu Rass is optimistic the Eisenkot-led opposition will ultimately accept Arab parties as partners in some fashion.

“If the Arabs get 15, 16, 17 MKs [members of the Knesset], everybody will knock on the doors of the Arabs,” he said. “Publicly, they are not willing to say that … [but] I’m sure after the election, they will talk differently.”

An anti-Netanyahu coalition would not bring peace, said Abu Rass, who lost 38 relatives to Israeli attacks on Gaza, but it could be a brake on the worsening atrocities of the current government. “Before ending the occupation,” he added, “I want to save my people.”

Warning of another far-right government, Atamneh believes she has finally convinced her mother to vote.

“There’s bad, and then there’s extremely bad. We’d much rather have bad than extremely bad,” she said. “Even if I can prevent one death or one demolition order or anything like that, then it’s better than nothing.”

After a brief pause, she added: “But then you’re like – well, I’m just helping Israel reshape its image [as a democracy]. It feels like a dead end.”

articles.title: A California geologist spotted a strange object sticking out of a creek; a Google reverse image search suggested it was an Ice Age mastodon tooth at least 10,000 years old
articles.summary: A California geomorphologist surveying a creek for a habitat restoration project noticed an unusual object lying half in and half out of the water.
articles.body: A California geomorphologist surveying a creek for a habitat restoration project noticed an unusual object lying half in and half out of the water. Unsure what she had found, she turned to Google’s reverse image search for clues. The search suggested it might be a molar from an Ice Age mastodon, and a paleontologist later confirmed it. The tooth belonged to an ancient Pacific mastodon, a mammal that roamed North America thousands of years ago. It was found in a Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District (Midpen) preserve in San Mateo County, during work to improve habitat for threatened California red-legged frogs. Researchers are now working to establish its age and significance.A reverse image search pointed to the identificationBrigid Lynch, a geomorphologist with Balance Hydrologics, found the object while conducting field surveys for the habitat enhancement project. When a reverse image search suggested it could be a mastodon molar, Midpen and her team contacted paleontologists for confirmation.Wayne Thompson, a paleontologist with Pacific Paleontology, confirmed it as an upper left molar from a Pacific mastodon (Mammut pacificus). The tooth measures about 8.5 inches long, 7 inches deep and 3 inches wide, and it retains both its crown and roots.Thompson called it “the most complete mastodon molar from our area” and the most spectacular he has ever seen. Mastodon teeth are often found broken, which makes the condition of this one especially significant.The tooth is at least 10,000 years old, and may be much olderThe tooth is estimated to be at least 10,000 years old, but its precise age has not been established. Thompson told Fox News Digital it could be between 50,000 and 100,000 years old. Researchers at Stanford University’s Doerr School of Sustainability plan to analyze the tooth to learn more about its age, the animal’s diet and its environment.Pacific mastodons were large herbivores that lived in western North America during the Pleistocene epoch, which ended about 11,700 years ago. Although related to modern elephants, they differed from mammoths in several ways, including their teeth and feeding habits. Mastodons primarily browsed on leaves, shoots and other vegetation rather than grazing mainly on grasses.Pacific mastodons were identified as a species distinct from the American mastodon in 2019, following extensive study of mastodon bones found in Southern California.Stanford will keep and scan the fossilMidpen donated the fossil to Stanford University to support further scientific study. Stanford will also produce a 3D scan of the tooth for Midpen to use in educational outreach, which allows people to examine the specimen without handling the original.The fossil could help scientists understand the animals that once inhabited the Bay Area and the ecosystems in which they lived. Such discoveries provide clues about past biodiversity and environmental change.The discovery site will remain undisclosedMidpen is not revealing the exact location, so that visitors do not go looking for their own fossils. Thompson has said the tooth may have recently separated from a skull that remains buried at the site, though this has not been confirmed.The find also offers an unexpected link between ancient wildlife and modern conservation. Lynch came across the fossil while working on a project to improve habitat for the threatened California red-legged frog. A survey meant to support a species facing present-day pressures instead uncovered evidence of an animal that disappeared thousands of years ago.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Russia targets European firms over Ukraine, largely spares US businesses as Putin-Trump ties warm
articles.summary: Russia is increasingly targeting European firms over their countries’ support for Ukraine, while largely sparing US businesses as Moscow seeks closer
articles.body: Russia is increasingly targeting European firms over their countries’ support for Ukraine, while largely sparing US businesses as Moscow seeks closer economic ties with Washington. A report suggested that only three of the 20 foreign-owned companies placed under Russian administration since US president Donald Trump took office in January 2025 were linked to the US.The remaining companies were controlled by European firms, highlighting the disparity in how Moscow has treated Western businesses amid the war in Ukraine and its efforts to improve economic ties with the Trump administration.A person close to Russian financial regulators told news agency Reuters that, with business negotiations under way with Washington, Moscow had little incentive to adopt the same hard line towards US firms as it had towards European businesses.The latest seizures include local units of Swiss food group Nestle and retailers Auchan and Metro. Russia also took control of assets belonging to four smaller companies from France, Germany, Sweden and Belgium last week.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the companies’ countries of origin were among the factors considered. He accused the countries involved of “illegal expropriations of Russian property”.A spokesperson for Switzerland’s State Secretariat for Economic Affairs said available information supported the perception that more European than US firms were being targeted. The European Commission described the recent seizures as “forced expropriation in all but name”.“This follows a clear pattern of economic retaliation,” a Commission spokesperson told Reuters, adding that the actions showed “Russia is not a safe environment for business”.Moscow courts US investmentThe contrast comes as contacts between Moscow and the Trump administration have intensified. US special envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday for talks on the Ukraine war. Russian news agencies reported that Putin expressed interest in restoring economic ties with Washington.Trump had announced a deal with Putin to resume Russian diesel supplies to US and global markets, with Russia set to dispatch its first cargo to the US on Thursday, Reuters reported. Trump also signed an executive order waiving key Russia-related sanctions and tariffs before they took effect under a new law, saying the move was in the US national interest.Russian negotiator Kirill Dmitriev, head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), has advocated the return and expansion of US businesses. He said last week that Russia and the US would soon announce joint initiatives that could proceed before the war ends.Trump has also taken steps aimed at easing economic restrictions on Russia, including signing an executive order on Saturday waiving key sanctions and tariffs on Russian goods, according to the report.Two US business people in Moscow told Reuters that Trump’s commitment to economic cooperation and ongoing negotiations had helped protect American companies. American Chamber of Commerce Russia president Robert Agee had previously summed up US business sentiment by saying: “We have Trump and they don't, and our hopes are linked to him.”US detainee released during envoy’s visitSeparately, Russia on Wednesday released Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American who had been jailed for more than four years on charges of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine. Hubbard’s legal team denied the allegations, while the US government under former president Joe Biden had designated him wrongfully detained.Trump said he had asked Putin to release Hubbard and that the US had not needed to free anyone in exchange. “He is the happiest man around,” Trump said, describing Hubbard as a “very high-quality, innocent man”.You use AI every day. articles.title: A city in South Korea seeks new ways to free a huge gray shark after it slips back into canal
articles.summary: The South Korean port city of Busan is trying to come up with a new way to free a huge dusky shark that swam back into a narrow canal hours after being freed.
articles.body: SEOUL, South Korea — A city in South Korea is trying on Thursday to come up with a new way to free a huge dusky shark out of a narrow canal. Workers in the port city of Busan had herded the shark, nicknamed Bukangi, out of the canal the day before, after weeks of trial and error — only for it to swim right back in hours later. Now Busan authorities and the country’s Oceans and Fisheries Ministry are determined to guide Bukangi back to open water, saying it is critical for the shark’s safety and health. The unconventional rescue effort on Wednesday involved dozens of workers maneuvering a floating platform through the canal to push the 9.8-foot female dusky shark out. After lingering in nearby waters for hours, the shark swam beneath an outer barrier net installed on the platform that night and re-entered the waterway. According to officials, Bukangi is now stuck between that net and a second one about 55 yards into the mouth of the canal, with on-site inspectors and rescuers debating ways to guide it back out as the shark circles the small patch of water. Lee Gwang-seok, an official with the Oceans and Fisheries Ministry, said Bukangi was unlikely to slip past more barriers and move farther up the canal, considering the density of the nets and the narrow waterway in that section that leaves little room for the shark to squeeze through. There were no signs that the shark had been feeding regularly during its monthlong stay in the canal, and falling water temperatures could pose additional health risks, officials say. Local Busan authorities did not immediately say when a new rescue effort for Bukangi would proceed. Sharing the Korean name of Busan’s North Port, where it was first spotted in mid-September, Bukangi had become a major tourist attraction as it slowly circled the canal, its fins slicing through the water’s surface. Busan officials, who made Bukangi a city mascot, say the shark attracted more than 1.7 million visitors to the canal, and hundreds of people lined up on the canal on Wednesday to watch the unusual rescue effort. Wednesday’s operation was the third attempt to free Bukangi, following failed efforts on Sept. 29 and Oct. 2 that involved boats spraying streams of water and nets placed across the narrow waterway. Bukangi avoided the boats and swam over the nets.

articles.title: Russian strikes hit Kyiv after Witkoff meets Putin
articles.summary: Ukraine says ‘appeasement’ will not end war as Russian attacks kill 1, injure 22 in its capital.
articles.body:
Russia and Ukraine have traded a new barrage of attacks after a United States envoy met Russia’s president in St Petersburg to push for renewed talks on ending the war.

Russian attacks on Kyiv overnight into Thursday killed at least one person and injured 22, including four children, Ukraine’s national emergency service said.

Metro infrastructure was also damaged at the Pivdenny Bridge, which spans the Dnipro River, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.

In Russia, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said two people were wounded after Ukraine launched a barrage of 630 drones on the region, 163 of which were sent to the capital city. He said most of the drones were intercepted.

The governor of the nearby Tula region said Russian air defences destroyed 70 drones. Another man was wounded in the Lipetsk region, its governor said.

The exchange of attacks came after US special envoy Steve Witkoff met with Russian President Vladimir Putin at Constantine Palace in St Petersburg on Wednesday.

During Witkoff’s visit, Russia released jailed US teacher Stephen Hubbard as a goodwill gesture, prompting the US envoy to praise Putin as a “humanitarian”.

US President Donald Trump later said he believed the Russia-Ukraine war may be as close as it’s ever been to ending.

But the Kremlin was more guarded. While it said Moscow was “in principle” willing to restart US-mediated talks with Ukraine, it warned there was little “substance” in Ukrainian and European peace proposals.

In recent days, a frustrated Trump has once again pivoted away from Ukraine and back to Putin, trumpeting what he said was a deal for heavily sanctioned Russia to sell diesel and reduce fuel prices sent soaring by the US-Israel war on Iran.

Trump also delayed a new wave of Russia-related sanctions, a decision he defended on Wednesday as necessary to secure Hubbard’s release.

Witkoff told Putin Washington was “grateful” for the diesel deal, which sparked outrage in Kyiv and across Europe.

The war, Europe’s worst since World War II, has killed tens of thousands of people since Russia’s full-scale February 2022 invasion of its neighbour.

Putin has consistently rejected face-to-face talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and insisted Moscow intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha on Thursday said “appeasement” would not stop Russia’s war campaign.

“Appeasement, servility, and flattery will not stop this war,” he wrote in a post on X. “Only strength will.”

articles.title: 'Beacon of hope': Polish PM Donald Tusk hails ties with India, calls PM Modi a 'friend'

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk on Thursday described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a “beacon of hope” amid global uncertainty and said he was proud to call him a friend, while highlighting the absence of conflicts of interest between India and Poland as the two countries seek to strengthen their strategic partnership.Addressing a joint press conference with PM Modi at Hyderabad House in New Delhi, Tusk said the two countries had held fruitful discussions on expanding bilateral cooperation and building on the strategic partnership established during Modi’s visit to Poland in August 2024.“We had a fruitful discussion with Prime Minister Modi about how Poland and India can develop and strengthen their strategic partnership. The decision to establish this partnership was made jointly during Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Warsaw in August 2024,” Tusk said.VIDEO | Delhi: Addressing a joint press meet with PM Narendra Modi, Polish PM Donald Tusk says, "We had a fruitful discussion with Prime Minister Modi about how Poland and India can develop and strengthen their strategic partnership. The decision to establish this partnership was made jointly during Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Warsaw in August 2024…The synergies between Poland and India are quite clear. We have no conflicts of interest and no historical issues that divide us. We are building our friendship on the basis of trust, shared values, and ideas such as non-violence. The great Polish Solidarity movement was based on non-violent action, and we were very much inspired by your tradition. This is quite obvious. We value and appreciate the global role that you, Prime Minister, play on the world stage. It is a source of hope in these times of destabilisation, uncertainty, political uncertainty, and instability.”(Source: Third Party)(Full video available on PTI Videos - Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) October 22, 2026“The synergies between Poland and India are quite clear. We have no conflicts of interest and no historical issues that divide us. We are building our friendship on the basis of trust, shared values, and ideas such as non-violence,” he added.Tusk also drew a parallel between Poland’s Solidarity movement and India’s tradition of non-violence, saying the Polish movement had been inspired by such principles.Praising PM Modi’s role on the global stage, the Polish prime minister said India’s leadership offered hope at a time of geopolitical uncertainty and instability.“Someone like you, Prime Minister, leading a country as powerful as India, is a beacon of hope for all of us. I am very proud, truly proud, to be able to call myself your friend, Mr. Prime Minister,” Tusk said.VIDEO | Delhi: Addressing a joint press meet with PM Narendra Modi, Polish PM Donald Tusk says, "Someone like you, Prime Minister, leading a country as powerful as India, is a beacon of hope for all of us. I am very proud, truly proud, to be able to call myself your friend, Mr. Prime Minister. Over the past 35 years, both our countries have experienced unprecedented economic success and dynamic growth. Let me put it straightforwardly, without any doubts or hesitation: the world looks upon us with envy, at how India is developing and at Poland’s development.”(Source: Third Party)(Full video available on PTI Videos - Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) October 22, 2026He also pointed to the economic progress made by both countries over the past 35 years.“Over the past 35 years, both our countries have experienced unprecedented economic success and dynamic growth. Let me put it straightforwardly, without any doubts or hesitation: the world looks upon us with envy, at how India is developing and at Poland’s development,” he said.PM Modi highlights opportunities from India-EU trade pactPM Modi said the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) had expanded opportunities for economic cooperation between India and Poland, building on the momentum in bilateral relations over the past two years.“Our growing economic strength has created new opportunities for the India-Poland partnership. And the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement has made these opportunities even broader,” PM Modi said.The two leaders witnessed the exchange of key memoranda of understanding before addressing the joint press conference.Welcoming Tusk, PM Modi recalled his visit to Poland in 2024, when the two countries elevated their relationship to a strategic partnership.“During that visit, we elevated our relations to the level of a Strategic Partnership. Building on this strong foundation, our partnership has gained new momentum over the past two years,” Modi said.He also highlighted the historical ties between the two countries, describing their friendship as rooted in shared humanity and empathy rather than diplomatic relations alone.“The friendship between India and Poland is not based merely on diplomatic relations, but on the shared heritage of humanity and empathy,” Modi said.Recalling the assistance extended to Polish families during the Second World War, PM Modi said the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter to thousands of Polish children and families in India.The prime minister also said the two sides had agreed to strengthen cooperation in culture, education, sports and tourism. He added that they had discussed regional and global developments, democratic values and the need to reform global governance institutions.“Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace,” PM Modi said.Trade, defence and technology on agendaTusk arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday for an official visit from October 21 to 23, at PM Modi’s invitation. He is accompanied by Poland’s minister of finance and economy Andrzej Domanski and a business delegation.The two prime ministers held delegation-level talks at Hyderabad House to review bilateral relations and explore cooperation across trade, defence, technology, space and other areas.India’s delegation included external affairs minister S Jaishankar, national security adviser Ajit Doval and foreign secretary Vikram Misri.Earlier on Thursday, Tusk paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat, laying a wreath at the memorial. Jaishankar also called on the Polish prime minister to discuss ways to deepen bilateral cooperation.In a post on X, Jaishankar said, “Pleased to call on Prime Minister Donald Tusk @donaldtuskof Poland. Appreciated his sharing thoughts on deepening India - Poland cooperation across a wide range of domains.”During his visit, Tusk is scheduled to attend the India-Poland Business Forum in New Delhi before travelling to Bengaluru on October 23 for engagements with leaders from India’s information technology and space sectors.Former Polish ambassador to India Adam Burakowski has said both countries aim to increase annual bilateral trade from approximately $6 billion to $10 billion.He has also identified defence and space technology as key areas for cooperation and pointed to the India-EU trade agreement as an opportunity to expand economic engagement.Tusk’s visit marks the first visit by a Polish prime minister to India since 2010. The two countries established their strategic partnership during PM Modi’s visit to Poland in August 2024.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
